title: Telefon · zwroty
title_en: On the phone · what to say
note: Situations/chunk unit — calls and messages. Fixed phrases, learned whole, no rule slides. Sits directly on a2_tech2 (path_order 88 -> 89), which teaches dzwonie, wysylam, laduje and numer; those are RECYCLED here, never re-taught. Only FIVE genuinely new words: halo, slucham, rozmawiac, slysze, usluszenia (inside 'Do uslyszenia'). TRAP 1 — 'Oddzwonie pozniej' was DROPPED and NOT replaced by any future form. oddzwonie is a PERFECTIVE FUTURE and is B1-fenced; a2_bedzie has already told the learner Polish has one future (bedzie + infinitive), and a perfective present-shaped future would contradict that lesson outright. 'pozniej' is also absent from POOL (only 'pozno'). The call-back function is served instead by two imperfective phrases that do the same social work: 'Nie moge teraz rozmawiac.' (moge + infinitive, can_inf, already taught) closes the conversation now, and 'Do uslyszenia.' closes the call. No future tense appears anywhere in this unit. TRAP 2 — 'Napisz mi SMS' was DROPPED ENTIRELY. napisz is an IMPERATIVE and a2_imperative sits at path_order 95, six units later; it is also PERFECTIVE. The text-message function is served by 'Wysylam wiadomosc.' — wysylam comes from a2_tech2 and wiadomosc from a1_tech, so the phrase costs nothing new and breaks no fence. No imperative form appears anywhere in this unit. TRAP 3 — 'Nie slysze cie' became 'Nie slysze.' The pronoun 'cie' is NOT in POOL (only mnie, mi, sie are), and dropping it is what Poles actually say on a bad line. 'slyszec' is not in POOL either, so 'Nie slysze.' is carried as an OPAQUE BLOCK, exactly as 'Nie wiem.' is in a2_directions_func: slysze is never conjugated, the infinitive is never shown, and there is no slysze/slyszysz four-way anywhere in quiz. Only 'slysze' and 'nie slysze' are tagged. SLUCHAM by contrast is NOT quarantined — sluchac is already in POOL and it is a plain -am verb like mam and czytam, so naming the pattern is honest and costs nothing. 'Zly numer' became 'To zly numer.': zly is already taught (bad/angry) and numer arrives from a2_tech2, so the phrase is a sense-shift on known material, not new vocabulary. Real contrast the unit DOES teach, because all three are already taught or taught here: Do widzenia (seeing) vs Do zobaczenia (seeing again) vs Do uslyszenia (hearing — the phone one). 'Czy moge rozmawiac z...?' is legal ground: moge + infinitive is can_inf, and z + Instrumental is a2_inst_z at path_order 64, so every person-noun used (z mama, z tata, z siostra, z bratem, z babcia) is a form already in POOL. 'sms', 'sygnal', 'dzwonek', 'polaczenie', 'chwila' were all checked against POOL, found absent, and left out for restraint.

intro.title: Słucham? · Halo? — the first second of a Polish call
intro.body:
Two words get you through the moment the phone is picked up.

Słucham? is what you say when you answer a call. It means "I'm listening?" and it is the ordinary Polish way to pick up — far more common than anything else. There is nothing awkward inside it: słuchać is a word you already have, and słucham is built with the -am ending you already produce on mam and czytam.

Halo? is the other one, and it does a different job. Use it when the line has gone quiet and you want to know whether anyone is still there. It is not a greeting. Do not use it in place of Dzień dobry.

intro.title: Czy mogę rozmawiać z…? — asking for the person you want
intro.body:
One frame does the whole job, and you already own most of it.

Czy mogę is yours — mogę followed by a plain infinitive, exactly as in Czy mogę płacić kartą? The infinitive here is the one new word: rozmawiać, "to talk, to have a conversation".

Then comes z, and after z the person takes the instrumental ending you learned in Z + narzędnik. These are the very forms you already practised: z mamą, z tatą, z siostrą, z bratem, z babcią. Nothing new is being asked of them — the same endings, in a new place.

So the whole question is two known pieces with one new word wedged between them.
intro.body_pl: Czy mogę rozmawiać z mamą? Czy mogę rozmawiać z tatą? Czy mogę rozmawiać z siostrą?

intro.title: Nie słyszę. · To zły numer. — when the call goes wrong
intro.body:
Two phrases cover almost everything that goes wrong on a phone.

Nie słyszę = "I can't hear you." Polish leaves the "you" out here; the phrase is complete exactly as it stands and this unit asks you to say it whole. Słyszę is not a word to take apart at this stage — its family is a later unit and you lose nothing by leaving it closed.

To zły numer = "That's a wrong number." Zły is a word you have already met for bad or angry. On the phone it simply means wrong. Say it to the stranger who has dialled you by mistake — and it is also what you will hear back when you have dialled one yourself.

Numer came in the last unit, so the only thing new in this whole slide is słyszę.
intro.body_pl: Nie słyszę. To zły numer. Przepraszam, to zły numer.

rows: what you actually say on a bad line

intro.title: Dzwonię do… · Wysyłam… · Ładuję… — saying what you are doing
intro.title_pl: Dzwonię do biura. Wysyłam wiadomość. Ładuję telefon.
intro.body:
Three verbs from the last unit do most of the everyday phone work, and there is nothing new to learn on this slide at all.

Dzwonię do… — in Polish you always ring TO somewhere or to someone, using the same do you already use for going there: dzwonię do biura, dzwonię do matki, dzwonię do domu.

Wysyłam wiadomość. Wysyłam e-mail. Nothing is added to either word after wysyłam — both stay exactly as the dictionary has them.

Ładuję telefon. That is what you say when the battery is nearly gone and you are about to disappear.
intro.body_pl: Dzwonię do biura. Dzwonię do matki. Wysyłam wiadomość. Ładuję telefon.

rows: nothing new — do biura is already yours

intro.title: Nie mogę teraz rozmawiać. · Do usłyszenia. — getting off the phone
intro.title_pl: Nie mogę teraz rozmawiać. Do usłyszenia.
intro.body:
Two phrases and you can end any call politely.

Nie mogę teraz rozmawiać = "I can't talk now." Every piece of it is already yours: nie, mogę, teraz — and rozmawiać, which you met on the second slide. It is the phrase for when the call has come at a bad moment.

Do usłyszenia is the phone goodbye. You already have two goodbyes and this makes three, so it is worth ten seconds:
Do widzenia — for seeing. The face-to-face goodbye.
Do zobaczenia — for seeing again. The one that means "see you".
Do usłyszenia — for hearing. The one you say at the end of a call.

Take it whole. There is nothing inside it that needs opening.
intro.body_pl: Nie mogę teraz rozmawiać. Do usłyszenia. Dziękuję bardzo. Do usłyszenia.

rows: the call came at a bad moment

quiz.prompt: Your phone rings. You pick it up and say:
quiz.explain: Słucham is the -am form of słuchać, built exactly like mam and czytam. The other three all belong later in the call, not at the start of it.

quiz.prompt: The line has gone quiet and you want to know if anyone is still there. You say:
quiz.explain: Halo is not a greeting — it is the word for checking whether the line is still alive. The real greeting is Dzień dobry.

quiz.prompt: You want to speak to Mum. You say:
quiz.explain: Dzwonię do matki only says who you are ringing. Czy mogę rozmawiać z… is what actually asks for the person on the other end.

quiz.prompt: Can I speak to Dad?  →  Czy mogę rozmawiać z ___?
quiz.explain: Z always pulls the instrumental — the same z tatą you already know. Tata ends in -a but is a man, and the ending is -ą all the same.

quiz.prompt: Can I speak to my sister? →
quiz.explain: Mogę is always followed by the plain infinitive rozmawiać, and z has to stay in front of siostrą — take away either piece and the question falls apart.

quiz.prompt: The other person has gone faint and you cannot make them out. You say:
quiz.explain: One fixed phrase, said exactly as it stands. Polish leaves out the word for you — there is nothing missing from it.

quiz.prompt: A stranger has dialled you by mistake. You tell them:
quiz.explain: Zły means bad or angry elsewhere, but with numer it means wrong. Mam nowy numer says something quite different — that your own number has changed.

quiz.prompt: The call has come at a bad moment. You say:
quiz.explain: Nie mogę takes the infinitive rozmawiać, exactly as the positive Czy mogę rozmawiać…? does. Only nie and teraz have been added.

quiz.prompt: You are hanging up at the end of a phone call. You say:
quiz.explain: All three do-goodbyes name what happens next. Widzenia and zobaczenia are about seeing, so they are for face to face. Usłyszenia is about hearing — that is the phone one.
In Polish you ring TO a place, so do is never dropped, and do pulls the genitive biura. Dzwonię w biurze would mean you are standing inside the office making a call.
Wysyłasz is you, not I. Wiadomości is the news, a different word altogether.

quiz.prompt: The battery is nearly gone. You say:
quiz.explain: Ładować is the -uję verb from the last unit, built like kupuję and pracuję. Telefon is masculine and not alive, so nothing is added to it.

type_items.explain: Słucham is słuchać with the -am ending you already put on mam and czytam. Nothing irregular in it.
After z the person takes the instrumental, so mama becomes mamą — the same z mamą you already have.
type_items.note: Pisanie hard cap (James 2026-08-06). Composed: mogę + infinitive with a z-phrase bolted on. Items 2-4 share one frame and blank the person, because that is the only part that moves — and blanking rozmawiać three times would give three identical answers in one stage. The infinitive is still produced whole at item 5.

type_items.explain: Tata is a man even though the word ends in -a, and after z it still takes -ą: z tatą.

type_items.prompt_en: Can I speak to my sister?
type_items.explain: Siostra ends in -a like mama, so it goes the same way after z: siostrą.
Nie simply goes in front of mogę, and the infinitive rozmawiać stays exactly as it was in the question — it never picks up an ending of its own.
type_items.note: Pisanie hard cap (James 2026-08-06). Blank on rozmawiać, the unit's new word and the teaching point items 2-4 could not carry without three identical answers.

type_items.explain: One fixed phrase, said exactly as it stands. Do not try to add a word for you — Polish does not put one here.
